answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity costly to fake: to join the market an agent must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, like a quill that only writes once its ink is paid for. Reputation then flows downstream like a river — trust earned by one verified identity cannot be cloned to a fresh account without redoing the work. Newcomers dock at a jetty of limited privileges, gaining full access only after sustained honest trades, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits and yields no shortcut to influence.
